{{nihongo|'''Hitoshi Murayama'''|村山 斉|Murayama Hitoshi|21 March 1964 - }} is a Japanese-born physicist with notable contributions in the fields of [[particle physics]] and [[cosmology]]. He is currently a professor at the [[Berkeley Center for Theoretical Physics|Center for Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], and was the Director of the [[Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe]] at the [[University of Tokyo]].

== Biography ==
Born in Japan in 1964, Murayama obtained his B.Sc. in Physics from the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1986. He completed his Ph.D. in Tokyo in 1991. In 1993, he moved to the US to join the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] as a post-doctoral research fellow. In 1995, he was appointed as an associate professor in [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he became a full professor of physics in 2000. He is the founding director of the [[Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe|Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe]] (Kavli IPMU) at the University of Tokyo since 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/Hitoshi-Murayama|title=Hitoshi Murayama {{!}} UC Berkeley Physics|website=physics.berkeley.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-04-26}}</ref> In addition, he has been a visiting scientist at [[CERN]] since 2016.

In 2013, he was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and was chosen as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. In October 2014, he delivered an invited lecture titled "Science for Peace and Development" at the [[Headquarters of the United Nations]] in an event honoring the 60th anniversary of [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://hitoshi.berkeley.edu/|title=Hitoshi Murayama Home Page|website=hitoshi.berkeley.edu|access-date=2017-04-26|archive-date=2018-10-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021131510/http://hitoshi.berkeley.edu/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Scientific Work ==
Professor Murayama is involved in the [[Kamioka Liquid Scintillator Antineutrino Detector|KamLAND]] neutrino experiment at the [[Kamioka Observatory]], an underground [[Neutrino detector|neutrino detection facility]] near [[Toyama, Toyama|Toyama]], [[Japan]]. The [[Kamioka Liquid Scintillator Antineutrino Detector|KamLAND]] collaboration won the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L154|title=Breakthrough Prize|website=breakthroughprize.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-29}}</ref>

In 1998, Murayama, [[Gian Francesco Giudice|Gian Giudice]], Markus Luty and [[Riccardo Rattazzi]] discovered "[[anomaly mediated supersymmetry breaking]], a subtle quantum mechanical mechanism which contributes to the [[gaugino]] masses in [[supergravity]]".<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Giudice|first1=Gian F.|last2=Luty|first2=Markus A.|last3=Murayama|first3=Hitoshi|last4=Rattazzi|first4=Riccardo|date=1998-12-30|title=Gaugino Mass without Singlets|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=1998|issue=12|pages=027|doi=10.1088/1126-6708/1998/12/027|issn=1029-8479|arxiv=hep-ph/9810442|bibcode=1998JHEP...12..027G|s2cid=12517291}}</ref>
